title: Meaning above storage
description: Reduce a signed fraction step by step, serve two rectangle representations with one client, build a pair from functions, count where gcd work happens, then bound two resistors in parallel.

learned: State and test the laws a constructor and its selectors must satisfy.
Write a client that survives a change of representation, one layer at a time.
Build a pair out of functions alone.
Measure where an interface does its work, and see repeated uncertainty widen an interval.
recap.invariant: Constructed values satisfy the public laws; clients depend on those meanings rather than storage positions.
recap.complexity: For one fraction whose two parts are each read k times, eager reduction makes 1 gcd call and uncached lazy reduction makes 2k. These count calls to gcd, not the work inside it; drawing is excluded.
recap.common_mistake: Reaching past a selector into the tuple or dictionary behind it, or using one uncertain quantity twice in an interval formula.
in_real_programs: Python's fractions.Fraction reduces in its constructor and keeps the sign on the numerator: it divides both parts by math.gcd, negated when the denominator is negative (CPython Lib/fractions.py).

retrieval.question: Module 2: why can separate calls to a pair creator retain different captured values?
retrieval.answer: Each creator invocation provides its own defining environment; its returned function retains access to those bindings.
